mission: Outpost wall, exterior. Kael leans with arms folded, watching the Knights from outside. He speaks more than he has spoken in days: 'They built everything on one thing. Take it away and they don't know how to stand. That's not a lattice problem. That's a design problem.' He does not know what he has just said. Ben does not yet either.
why_now: Kael's arc-moment-of-truth. The resonance answer arrives in embryonic form, spoken by the least expected voice — the outsider naming what the insiders cannot see.
conflict: Kael has been watching the outpost from outside. What he sees is not the wound; it is the single-framework fragility his arc has always noticed. He says more than he usually says. Ben hears a sentence; he does not yet hear the answer inside it.
turning_point: Kael: 'They built everything on one thing. Take it away and they don't know how to stand. That's not a lattice problem. That's a design problem.' The chapter's second anchor-line lands.
opening_hook: Kael leans against the outpost wall with arms folded and watches the struggling Knights the way he watches everything — from outside, measuring, cataloging
closing_hook: Departure from the outpost. Close enough to feel the primary wound now — immense, pulling. Veranthos is ahead. The endgame approaches.
emotional_trajectory: Kael's quiet observation -> the insight landing -> grim departure

stakes.personal: Kael's insight arriving through outsider perspective
stakes.interpersonal: Kael engaging with the group's problem not from obligation but from honest observation

setting: Jedi outpost -> departure, approach toward Veranthos
sensory_details: The outpost shrinking behind them; the wound ahead pulling, immense, the wrongness concentrated into a gravity of absence; Kael's voice quiet and precise, the most words he has strung together in days; Veranthos's star visible on the nav display
action_beats: Kael leans against the outpost wall with arms folded, watching the struggling Knights from the outside
Kael speaks the most words he's strung together in days — quiet, precise, the outsider naming what insiders can't see
The group boards the Steady Returns for departure as the primary wound's pull grows ahead of them
notes: Kael's 'design problem' observation is the chapter's other anchor-line. Both Sera's 'What is your plan, Skywalker?' and Kael's 'that's a design problem' do immense work in small sentences. Anti-pattern: Ben does not, on-page, recognise Kael's line as the resonance answer — the reader registers it; Ben does not yet. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, paragraph the connection between Kael's sentence and Gavran's resonance note. The sentence sits in the air; the Codex bookmark is still open on his datapad; the chapter ends on approach.
